summary: Martin Seeger works in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 2004 under Barend Jan Terwiel, held a post there as of 2004, and served on the Pali Text Society Council as of 2026.

Martin Straube specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies and studied under Michael Hahn. As of 2026, he holds posts at the Göttingen Academy, International Institute for Buddhist Studies, University of Bristol, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Martin T. Adam works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and studied under teachers including Leslie S. Kawamura, Tom Tillemans, and Shoryu Katsura, later instructing at McGill.

Martin Willson (d. 2005) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Supervised for her MA by Lambert Schmithausen, she earned her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she has also held a post as a researcher.

Martine Kropman is an Indology scholar. She conducted doctoral research at the University of Groningen and is an external PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop as of 2026.
Martino Dibeltulo works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan, where he was supervised by Donald S. Lopez Jr., and was mentored by Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg (1922–2016) was an art historian and scholar. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954), and held a long-term post at the University of Michigan (~1949–1988).
Mary Anne Cartelli specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Philip Boas Yampolsky.

Mary Clabaugh Wright (1917–1970) was a sinologist and historian. Educated at Vassar College and Radcliffe College (PhD ~1939–1951), she curated Stanford's China collection (1947) before becoming associate professor (1959) and full professor (1964) at Yale University.

Mary Evelyn Tucker (b. 1949) is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Japanology who earned her PhD at Columbia University. She served as Professor of Religion at Bucknell University (~1989–2006) and became a professor at Yale University (~2006).

Mary Haas (1910–1996) was a linguist. She studied under Edward Sapir at the University of Chicago and Yale University, completing her studies in 1935, and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1941–1977).

Mary Jaksch (b. 1947) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland as a student of Peter Harvey, and also studied under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Mary Shepherd Slusser (1918–2017) was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. After earning degrees from the University of Michigan and Columbia University (PhD ~1950), she worked at the U.S. State Department and the National Museum of African Art.

Marybeth White works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed an honors double major degree at York University and pursued doctoral studies as a candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University.

Maryla Falk (1906–1980) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1937–1939) and was a member of the Polish Oriental Society and the Royal Asiatic Society.
Marylin Martin Rhie specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Mentored by Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, she served as a professor at Smith College.

Masaaki Chikusa (1930–2015) was a scholar of sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University (PhD 1980), he held assistant and associate posts there between 1968 and 1993, later becoming a professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).

Masaaki Hattori (b. 1924) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta, he taught at Kyoto University (1961–1988) and served as dean of letters at Hanazono University (~1994–1996).

Masaaki Nitta (b. 1936) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1962–1968) and served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (~1975–1992) and Fukui Prefectural University.
